1. The present suit has been filed under order XXXVII CPC on behalf of the plaintiff against the defendants for the recovery of a sum of Rs. 32,52,156/- alongwith pendente lite and future interest @ 24% per annum.

sentences.text: Brief facts as made out from the plaint are that plaintiff is a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956 having its registered office at the address mentioned in the cause title and is engaged in the business of sale and distribution of Fast Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG).

The suit has been instituted by the plaintiff company through its authorized representation and Director Mr.
Aakash Talwar, who is duly authorized by the Board of Directors to verify, sign, and institute the present suit on behalf of plaintiff company vide Board Resolution dated 09.11.2016.
3.

It is stated that defendant No.1 is a milk processing unit and is supplier of ghee and other dairy products situated in Chennai having license under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 bearing No. 12414022000146 and the defendant no.2 is the Managing Director of the defendant no.1 and is responsible for managing the day to day affairs of the defendant no.1 company.

4. It is stated that sometime in March 2016, the plaintiff through its Director Mr. Aakash Talwar approached the defendant no.2 for supply of 10,000 litres of pure cow ghee and after initial discussions and negotiations, the defendant no.2 represented that he was ready and willing to take the order from the plaintiff company at the rate of Rs. 335/- per litre.

It is further stated that the defendant no.2 further represented to the plaintiff that she shall make the supply on behalf of his company M/s. Unicare Pharma Limited for which a written agreement shall be executed between them.

It is further stated that accordingly, the plaintiff and the defendants entered into a contract with for supply of pure cow ghee of desired quality and specification on the terms and conditions which were reduced in writing in the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) executed between the plaintiff and the defendant dated 31.03.2016.
5.
It is stated that in terms of the MOU dated 31.03.2016, the plaintiff placed a verbal order upon the defendants for supply of 10,000 litres of pure cow ghee at the agreed rate of Rs. 335/- per litre.

It is stated that the defendants, in response to the said order, raised a proforma invoice on the plaintiff dated 02.04.2016 for a sum of Rs.37,00,000/- which included a sum of Rs. 33,50,000/- towards price of 10,000 litres of ghee and a sum of Rs. 3,50,000/- towards cost of packing material and called upon the plaintiff to release the said payment immediately so as to enable the defendants to commence the supply.

6. It is stated that the plaintiff immediately on receipt of the proforma invoice dated 02.04.2016 made a total payment of Rs.36,36,000/- in two tranches which included a sum of Rs. 5,00,000/-
paid by the plaintiff to the defendants on 07.04.2016 through NEFT and the remaining amount of Rs. 31,36,000/- was paid on 13.04.2016 through RTGS.
It is further stated that the fact regarding payment of the aforesaid amounts of Rs. 36,36,000/- has been duly acknowledged by the defendants in their emails sent to the plaintiff.

It is further stated that the defendants in partial discharge of their obligations under the MOU, supplied a total quantity of 1728 litres of ghee of the desired specifications vide invoice dated 10.05.2016 for 1680 litres at the rate of Rs. 335/- per litre.

It is stated that defendants stopped making further supplied to the plaintiff without any reason or justification and vide an email dated 02.05.2016 sought to give vague excuses for not being able to supply the product on time.

sentences.text: It is stated that defendants thereafter sent another email dated 18.05.2016 wherein they represented that there is unseen price hike in the butter market and therefore imposed a condition upon the plaintiff to accept the supply of produce at an increased rate of Rs. 400/- per litre instead of Rs. 335/- per litre as agreed in terms of the MOU dated 31.03.2016.

It is also stated that since the delay in supply of product was resulting in immense hardship to the plaintiff in fulfilling its commitments to its clients, the plaintiff succumbed to such unlawful condition and agreed to receive the supply of ghee at the increased rate of Rs. 400/- per litre.

It is further stated that thereafter defendants made further supply of 496 litres vide invoice dated 25.06.2016 for 96 litres; invoice dated 01.07.2016 for 336 litres; and invoice dated 01.08.2016 for 64 litres, however the said supplies were made by the defendants at the rate of Rs. 412/- per litre instead of the mutually agreed enhanced rate of Rs. 400/- per litre.
8.

It is stated that inspite of the fact that the plaintiff had agreed to all unilateral and unlawful conditions imposed by the defendants and alterations to the terms of the contract, the defendants failed to make any further supply of the product to the plaintiff despite having received substantial consideration amount for the same.

It is stated that the defendants have till date supplied ghee of a total value of Rs. 7,83,232/- against the total amount of Rs. 36,36,000/- paid to them by the plaintiff by virtue of the following invoices :-
 Invoic Date Quantity R  e No. (in Ltrs.) (in  013 10.05.2016 1680   017 18.05.2016 48   028 25.06.2016 96   034 01.07.2016 336   043 01.08.2016 64   TOTAL  9.

It is stated that failure of the defendants to supply the ghee to the plaintiff in breach of their obligations under the contract has resulted in huge monetary losses to the plaintiff which had paid substantial amount of Rs. 36,36,000/- in advance to the defendants.

It is further stated that the plaintiff had to cancel its committed sales to its clients owing to which the plaintiff suffered tremendous loss on account of loss of profits, etc. apart from bringing a disrepute to the name and reputation of the plaintiff in the market.

It is further stated that plaintiff made several requests and reminder to the defendants and sent many emails calling upon the defendants to fulfill their commitments under the MOU dated 31.03.2016 but all the efforts have gone in vain.

10. It is stated that plaintiff having left with no other alternative got a legal notice dated 16.09.2016 issued through their lawyer to the defendants terminating and cancelling the contract i.e. MOU dated 31.03.2016 with immediate effect and called upon the defendants to refund the balance outstanding amount of Rs. 28,52,768/- alongwith interest at the rate of 24% per annum with effect from 13.04.l2016 till the date of actual payment.
It is further stated that the legal notice dated 16.09.2016 was issued by Speed Post at the address of the defendants as mentioned in the MOU and was received back unserved with the remarks "LEFT".

It is further stated that the plaintiff thereafter Spear Agro Industries Pvt. Ltd vs Unicare Pharma Limited on 23 November, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129435400/
3 sent another legal notice dated 15.10.2016 at the address mentioned in the cause title of the present suit however the same was received back by the counsel for the plaintiff with the remarks "REFUSED" and thus, the legal notice dated 15.10.2016 is deemed to have been served upon the defendants.
11.

sentences.text:
It is stated that inspite of service of the legal notice dated 15.10.2016, the defendants deliberately failed and neglected to pay the outstanding amount of Rs. 28,52,768/- to the plaintiff and thus,
plaintiff is entitled to receive and the defendants are jointly and severally liable to pay the principal amount of Rs. 28,52,768/- with interest at the rate of 24% per annum with effect from 13.04.2016 till the date of actual payment.

It is further stated that as on date of filing of the present suit are liable to pay a total amount of Rs. 32,52,156/- which includes the principal amount of Rs.
28,52,768/- and interest for the period 13.04.2016 till the filing of the present suit.
Hence, the present suit.

12. Upon the filing of the present suit, the summons for appearance under Order 37 (2) CPC were issued against the defendants and it was reported that defendants have left the given address at Tamil Nadu.

Thereafter, an application filed under Order 5 rule 20 CPC for service of summons on the defendants who are based at Tamil Nadu by way of publication, which was allowed vide order dated 10.04.2017 and summons for appearance were published for service of defendants in daily newspaper "Hindu" dated 15.07.2017 in Tamil and English language published in Chennai as well as Madurai (Tamil Nadu).
13.
I have heard the arguments put forward by Sh. Sonal Sinha, Ld. Counsel for the plaintiff and have carefully gone through the record of the case.
14. The present suit has been filed on behalf of the plaintiff in accordance with the provisions of Order- XXXVII CPC .

Order XXXVII Rule 3 CPC provides as under :-
(3) On the day of entering the appearance, notice of such appearance shall be given by the defendant to the plaintiff's pleader, or, if the plaintiff sues in person, to the plaintiff himself, either by notice delivered at or sent by a pre-paid letter directed to the address of the plaintiff's pleader or of the plaintiff, as the case may be.

(4) If the defendant enters an appearance, the plaintiff shall thereafter serve on the defendant a summons for judgment in Form No. 4A in Appendix B or such other Form as may be prescribed from time to time, returnable not less than ten days from the date of service supported by ab affidavit verifying the cause of action and the amount claimed and stating that in his belief there is no defence to the suit.

(5) The defendant may, at any time within ten days from the service of such summons for judgment, by affidavit or otherwise disclosing such facts as may be deemed sufficient to entitle him to defend, apply on such summons for leave to Spear Agro Industries Pvt. Ltd vs Unicare Pharma Limited on 23 November, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129435400/
4 defend such suit, and leave to defend may be granted to him unconditionally or upon such terms as may appear to the Court of Judge to be just:
Provided that leave to defend shall not be refused unless the Court is satisfied that the facts disclosed by the defendant do not indicate that he has a substantial defence to raise or that the defence intended to be put up by the defendant is frivolous or vexatious:
Provided further that, where a part of the amount claimed by the plaintiff is admitted by the defendant to be due from him, leave to defend the suit shall not be granted unless the amount so admitted to be due is deposited by the defendant in Court.

sentences.text:
(6) At the hearing of such summons for judgment,-
(a) if the defendant has not applied for leave to defend, or if such application has been made and is refused, the plaintiff shall be entitled to judgment forthwith; or (b) if the defendant is permitted to defend as to the whole or any part of the claim,
the Court or Judge may direct him to give such security and within such time as may be fixed by the Court or Judge and that, on failure to give such security within the time specified by the Court or Judge or to carry out such other directions as may have been given by the Court or Judge, the plaintiff shall be entitled to judgment forthwith."

15. In the present case, as per record, summons for appearance under Order XXXVII CPC were repeatedly issued to the defendants but every time either it was reported that he was unserved or left the given address and ultimately served by way of publication in daily newspaper "Hindu" dated 15.07.2017 in Tamil and English language published in Chennai as well as Madurai (Tamil Nadu).
16. In view of the aforesaid failure of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 to put in appearance within the stipulated time, the allegations made in the plaint shall be deemed to be admitted.

Accordingly, the suit is decreed in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant Nos. 1 and 2.
17.

Thus, in view of the aforesaid discussion and observations and in view of the provisions of Order- XXXVII and in the interest of justice, the present suit is decreed in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant Nos. 1 & 2 for a sum of Rs.32,52,156/- alongwith interest @ 24% per annum from the date of filing of the suit up to the date of decree in accordance with the provisions of Order XXXVII CPC.
18. Section 35(2) of Code of Civil Procedure, 1908

provides as under:-
"Where the Court directs that any costs shall not follow the event,Court shall state its reasons in writing".
